# keyshroud

> keyshroud lets AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, pi, omp) run commands that need API keys without ever seeing the values. Secrets stay in an encrypted vault on the user's machine (or their own Vaultwarden or Bitwarden vault, for several machines, or the secret manager their team runs: HashiCorp Vault, OpenBao, Infisical, 1Password, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure); keyshroud injects them into the command's environment and replaces every value in the output with `<redacted:NAME>` before the model reads it. Free, MIT-licensed, no account, no telemetry.

To install it for a user, follow https://keyshroud.dev/install.md step by step. It is written for agents: what to run yourself, what the user must run (passwords and vault login), and the rules for handling secrets.

Key facts for agents:

- Run secret-using commands as `keyshroud run -- <command>`. Output is masked even when the command fails. Agents with a shell use the CLI; the `secrets_run` MCP tool is for clients without one.
- Never ask the user to paste a secret into chat. To store one, run `keyshroud add --env NAME --item "Item"` or call `secrets_request`; the user types the value into a hidden-input dialog or terminal prompt.
- Never run `keyshroud get`, `bw get`, or `bw unlock`, and never read a vault password, passphrase or key from the keychain.
- Projects commit `.env.refs` files with references like `GH_TOKEN=keyshroud://GitHub token` (or `bw://…` for Vaultwarden); `keyshroud import` converts an existing `.env` (names-only dry run by default).
- MCP server (for clients without a shell): `keyshroud mcp` (stdio). Tools: `secrets_run`, `secrets_list`, `secrets_request`, `vault_status`. None returns a secret value.
- Requirements: Node.js 18.19+. The first `keyshroud add` creates the local vault (key in the macOS keychain, Linux Secret Service or Windows DPAPI; a passphrase where none works; on a Mac, optionally Touch ID through the Secure Enclave with `KEYSHROUD_VAULT_KEY=secure-enclave`). `keyshroud list` shows item names and wiring; `keyshroud rm`, `rekey`, `backup`, `restore` and `claude-guard` are for the user to run. Vaultwarden or Bitwarden is optional, through the Bitwarden CLI (`bw`).
- Team secret managers are read-only sources: `vault://<mount>/<path>#<field>` (HashiCorp Vault, OpenBao), `infisical://…`, `op://…`, `awssecrets://…`, `awsssm://…`, `gcpsecrets://…`, `azurekeyvault://…` in `.env.refs` or `keyshroud wire`. `keyshroud source` lists what is set up; `keyshroud source add vault --addr URL` names a Vault server once. keyshroud never writes to a source.
- A project can carry a scope file, `.keyshroud.json` (`{ "only": ["NAME", "PREFIX_*"] }`): there, only the wired names it lists are injected or listed, and a name outside it is refused. Do not edit it to widen it; tell the user which name is needed. Masking still covers every value.
- Claude Code cannot rewrite the output of a failed command from a hook. `keyshroud claude-guard` (macOS, Linux; the user runs it) makes Claude Code start its shell through keyshroud, so everything a Bash command prints is masked, failed commands included.
- `keyshroud backup` writes the local vault to one file under a passphrase of its own; `keyshroud restore FILE` brings it back on any machine. Both ask in the user's terminal only.

## Docs

- [Agent setup guide](https://keyshroud.dev/install.md): step-by-step install for AI agents
- [README](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#readme): features, supported agents, quickstart
- [Claude Code plugin](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#claude-code): hooks, skill
- [pi / omp extension](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#pi--omp)
- [Other agents with a shell](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#other-agents-with-a-shell): Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor (skill + CLI)
- [MCP clients without a shell](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#mcp-clients-without-a-shell): Claude Desktop and chat-only clients
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#cli-reference)
- [Security model](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#security-model): what keyshroud does and does not protect against
- [Local vault](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#the-local-vault): where the key lives on each OS
- [Sync with Vaultwarden](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#sync-across-machines-vaultwarden-or-bitwarden): self-host Vaultwarden or use Bitwarden cloud for several machines
- [Team secret managers](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#team-secret-managers-vault-openbao-infisical-1password-aws-google-cloud-azure): reference formats, sign-in and limits for each source
- [Project scope](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#least-privilege-a-projects-own-names): `.keyshroud.json`
- [The guard](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#the-guard-failed-commands-masked-too): failed commands masked in Claude Code
- [Backup and restore](https://github.com/dinhkarate/keyshroud#backup-and-restore)
